issue_paraphrase: Running poetry's debug resolve command on a dependency that is restricted to certain platforms (for example a package that only supports a particular operating system) crashes with an index-out-of-range error right after printing the resolution summary, so the user gets a Python traceback instead of the dependency listing with its platform marker. The crash happens only for packages that carry such an environment marker, because the command mistakenly assumes the result row it builds already has a third column and assigns to it instead of appending.
fix_summary: DebugResolveCommand built a two-element row [name, version] and then did `row[2] = str(pkg.marker)` for packages whose marker is not 'any'; assignment to the nonexistent index 2 raised IndexError. The fix appends the marker with row.append(str(pkg.marker)).
notes: Fully offline, ~0.2s per direction. No network needed. Run with `-o addopts=""` because poetry's pyproject.toml sets xdist/randomly addopts. poetry-core MUST be pinned to the exact lock ref or `pip install -e .` will pull poetry-core main and can drift. The regression test uses the tests/console/conftest.py CommandTester fixtures (repo fixture is an in-memory TestRepository; nothing external).

issue_paraphrase: When a poetry configuration value is used inside another config value's string template (a value of the form {some.config.key}), any value that is falsy -- zero, False, or an empty string -- is treated as if the referenced key were unset, so the placeholder is left literally unexpanded in the resolved value. Users who legitimately configure zero or false for things like retry counts see the raw template text where a concrete value should appear.
fix_summary: In Config.process(), the interpolation callback tested `if config_value:` (falsy lookup values treated as missing) and returned the non-str value directly; fixed to `if config_value is not None:` plus str(config_value) for re.sub compatibility, and corrected the return annotation.

issue_paraphrase: When a git dependency is specified by an explicit ref such as refs/heads/somebranch or refs/tags/v1.0, poetry's legacy clone routine runs `git checkout` with the raw ref unchanged instead of with the plain branch or tag name. The intended normalization never happens because the code stored the result of the string-stripping call nowhere and also looked for the refs prefix under a misspelled name, so the checkout either fails or lands on the wrong revision for such dependencies.
fix_summary: Git._clone_legacy() called revision.replace('refs/head/', '') twice without assigning the result (so no stripping ever happened) and used the misspelled refs/head/ path; fixed by assigning revision = revision.removeprefix('refs/heads/') and revision = revision.removeprefix('refs/tags/') before SystemGit.checkout.

issue_paraphrase: If an install fails during the build step and the project defines single-string build settings (for example an environment-variable-style setting like CC=gcc) under the build-config-settings configuration, the remediation pip command that poetry prints in the error message is garbled: the string value is treated as a list of its individual characters, producing a run of nonsensical options like a flag per letter instead of one option for the whole setting. Arrays of settings survive, only plain-string settings are mangled, so the user cannot copy the shown command to retry the build.
fix_summary: In Executor's error-path pip command construction, iterate `config_settings[setting]` only after wrapping a plain str value in a list (`values = config_settings[setting]; if isinstance(values, str): values = [values]`), so string values are rendered as one --config-settings=<key>=<value> flag instead of one per character.

issue_paraphrase: Poetry's dependency resolver shows a small progress indicator with a stack of 'operation' contexts while it works. If resolving a dependency fails mid-operation (for instance a network or resolution error inside the indicator's scope), the label of the aborted operation is never removed, so the stale context leaks out of its with-block and keeps being displayed on later, unrelated progress lines. The cleanup only runs on the happy path.
fix_summary: Indicator.context() cleaned up the Indicator.CONTEXT class variable only after a normal yield-return; wrapped the yield in try/finally so the context is always cleared, including when the body raises.
notes: Fully offline, ~0.1s per direction.
